candidates.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
candidates.abstract: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations. Here we use quantum simulation to investigate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction, spanning strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. Using 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, we evolve initially localized strings with static or dynamical endpoint charges. Spatially resolved measurements reveal rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation in the string interior near the pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields. String-path occupations further probe transverse rearrangements between configurations connected by plaquette operations. Retaining separate matter and gauge degrees of freedom makes local Gauss-law constraints directly accessible for error detection. Combining these constraints with ancilla checks and noise rescaling, we measure dynamics in circuits containing up to 15 second-order Trotter steps. Our results establish quantum simulation as a practical approach to exploring nonperturbative string dynamics in two spatial dimensions, with gauge redundancy serving as an experimental resource.

candidates.title: A Statistical Analysis of Lopsidedness in Disk Galaxies
candidates.abstract: We present a statistical analysis of Fourier lopsidedness in disk galaxies based on a deduplicated compilation of 606 unique objects: 442 have a measured m = 1 amplitude (A1), and 302 of these also have a measured m = 2 amplitude (A2), with no entry carrying A2 alone. The sample is a factor of approximately 3 larger than earlier homogeneous A1-A2 datasets. Our main results are: (i) Both A1 and A2 follow log-normal distributions (KS D = 0.046 and 0.048) which are strongly preferred over Rayleigh or exponential forms, pointing to a multiplicative amplification process rather than random-phase superposition. (ii) The m = 1 and m = 2 modes are correlated as A2 = 0.29 A1 + 0.11 (Spearman rho = 0.501, p less than 10^-19). (iii) A1 rises monotonically with morphological T-type from approximately 0.07 in E/S0 to approximately 0.37 in Sm/Im galaxies (Kendall tau = 0.234, p approximately 10^-12). (iv) A1 anti-correlates with gas rotation velocity (Spearman rho = -0.432) and, in a stellar-mass cross-matched subsample of 246 galaxies with independent stellar-mass estimates, with stellar mass (rho = -0.395). The weaker lopsidedness of massive, fast-rotating disks indicates that the observed m = 1 amplitude is regulated by internal dynamics rather than set by tidal perturbations alone. (v) The TNG50-1 simulation, analysed through the TNGGalaxyLab Fourier pipeline, reproduces the observed A1-stellar-mass anti-correlation with a nearly identical Spearman coefficient, although its median A1 is approximately 1.4 times lower, an offset consistent with the heterogeneous target selection of the observational compilation.

candidates.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
candidates.abstract: ```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

candidates.title: BoviShift: A Six-Year Multi-Attribute Audit of Visual Cattle Phenotyping Across Animals and Time
candidates.abstract: Computer vision offers a scalable, non-contact means of estimating livestock traits, but correlated images and video frames make reliable evaluation difficult. Image-random splitting can place views of the same animal in both training and test sets, while deployment further requires transfer to animals captured in future years. We introduce BoviShift, a corpus reconstructed from six consecutive annual cohorts of an operational cattle marketplace collected from 2021 to 2026. It contains 2{,}657 cattle, 10{,}610 still images, and 2{,}566 walk-around videos across nine recorded breed categories. We evaluate three splitting strategies through four configurations: image-random and pooled cattle-disjoint splits over the same development cohorts, followed by separate future-2025 and locked future-2026 evaluations. Using a fixed ResNet-50 multi-task baseline, we assess weight, age, height, breed, and coat color. Differences between image-random and cattle-disjoint splitting are task-dependent rather than a universal leakage penalty. Future-cohort behavior is also attribute- and cohort-specific: breed declines relative to pooled evaluation; mean weight and age performance fails to beat constant baselines in 2025; height remains above baseline; and color transfers well to 2025 but degrades in 2026. Multi-task training improves all five point estimates in a single-seed ablation, still-view aggregation helps selectively, and zero-shot video-frame aggregation exposes a still-to-video domain gap. To our knowledge, BoviShift is the longest-spanning cattle-vision resource combining consecutive annual cohorts with physical and visual attributes.

candidates.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
candidates.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we study the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,1}$ as well as complements of star-shaped configurations of rational curves in K3 surfaces, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

candidates.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
candidates.abstract: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(β)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2β)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $β\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $β\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.

candidates.title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
candidates.abstract: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.

candidates.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
candidates.abstract: We study the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-θ}$, where $a>0$ and $θ\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $θ>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $θ<1$, polynomially when $θ=1$, and not at all when $θ>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $θ<1$ and, for $θ=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $θ=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $θ>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $θ\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $θ\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $θ=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.

candidates.title: SkipLane: Write-Once, Conflict-Free Accumulation for Zero-Skipping CNN Engines on FPGAs
candidates.abstract: Skipping zero activations saves multiplications in CNN accelerators, but it complicates accumulation: the products in a compressed input window belong to different output columns and must be merged. In our earlier engine, this merging was done by read-modify-write (RMW) of a row buffer, which made sparse inputs slower than dense ones even at 87% sparsity. Existing designs either merge kernel rows through RMW or reduce bank conflicts with extra hardware, without eliminating them. SkipLane makes the entire accumulation path write-once. Each kernel row is processed in its own lane, which holds partial sums in three registers and retires up to three finished columns per cycle into memory banks that cannot conflict. Lanes and input channels are summed only at readout, so no partial sum is ever read back. Multipliers left idle by zero weights compute a second filter in the same pass. In RTL simulation, the engine stays within 0.5% of its frontend bound up to 70% sparsity and is 1.10-1.26$\times$ faster than an SCNN-style scatter accumulator with 18 banks and ideal RMW at 50-80% sparsity. Six engines meet 140 MHz on a PYNQ-Z2 using 21.1k LUTs and run LeNet-5 bit-exact on the board. For conv1, the engine needs 1.94$\times$ fewer cycles than a dense engine (1.26$\times$ faster end to end); for conv2, whose rows are only 13 pixels wide, it reaches 0.87$\times$ the dense speed.

candidates.title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
candidates.abstract: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $Γ$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $Γ= 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

candidates.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
candidates.abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

candidates.title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
candidates.abstract: Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised. We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation. Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to naïve KM risks. The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.

candidates.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
candidates.abstract: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $Λ$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $Λ\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_δ$ and second-order $b_{δ^2}, b_{{G}_2}$. We also measure the running on halo catalogs based on full $N$-body simulations and show that the RG prediction describes the measurements well within the predicted systematic errors. Our results establish the RG flow as a natural formulation for relating galaxy bias measurements at different cutoffs and connecting the schemes used in field-level and $n$-point function analyses.

candidates.title: Dwarf galaxy simulations with stellar-core mass- and metallicity-dependent core-collapse supernova explosion energies
candidates.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are a critical source of thermal and kinetic energy and chemically enriched material in galaxies. Leveraging recent advances in CCSN modelling, we implement a novel core-mass- and metallicity-dependent prescription for stellar explodability and CCSN explosion energies, $E_\mathrm{expl}$, in the SPHGal galaxy evolution code. It accounts for black hole (BH) formation via SN failures and via partial fallback of ejecta mass, and adopts an explosion-progenitor connection calibrated to three-dimensional CCSN simulations, such that $E_\mathrm{expl}$ varies between $<0.1$-$2\, \mathrm{B}$. We ran simulations of isolated low-metallicity galaxies with variations in the input stellar feedback models. With the new explodability prescription nearly three times more BHs form compared to the canonical CCSN-model, but the reduced number of successful CCSNe has minimal impact on galactic star formation owing to the low fraction of failed CCSNe. While BH formation contributes to removal of matter from the galactic baryon cycle, the latter remains driven by galactic outflows, and most compact remnant mass is stored in white dwarves. The most significant change is instead brought about by the new average-$E_\mathrm{expl}$ that amounts to $\sim33$\% of the $1\,\mathrm{B}=10^{51}\, \mathrm{erg}$ traditionally assumed in sub-resolution CCSN-models. This reduction results in increased and less bursty star formation, reduced outflows and mass-loading factors, increased star cluster formation efficiency, and enhanced chemical enrichment and metal-recycling in star-forming regions. These results stand in contrast with outflow-launching and baryon cycle modelling in lower-resolution galaxy simulations in which canonical (i.e., $1\, \mathrm{B}$) CCSN feedback is typically assumed to produce galaxy models that match observed scaling relations.

candidates.title: Convergence and global optimality of Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao descent for Gaussian mixtures
candidates.abstract: We study explicit Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao descent for fitting Gaussian location mixtures by nonparametric maximum likelihood. The full sequence converges weakly and has finite length in the bounded-Lipschitz metric throughout the original step-size range. These conclusions hold for any fixed data set in any dimension and any initial probability measure. By an earlier conditional optimality theorem, the limit maximizes the likelihood under full-support initialization. Fix any particle step size in $(0,1]$. Initialize the particles by resampling the observations. For an open set of triples of points in the plane, the probability of convergence to a strictly suboptimal fixed point tends to one exponentially as the particle count grows. Without reweighting, a centered Gaussian initialization can give a strictly suboptimal limit. Every finite iterate has a smooth, strictly positive density. The limit assigns positive mass to a nonglobal local maximum of the associated Gaussian sum. We also give the exact pure-transport limit for a one-dimensional initialization with full support and an atom. An exact finite-dimensional representation preserves the truncated likelihood moments and the retained region's contribution to the current dissipation. This lets us transfer an analytic gradient inequality to the measure trajectory.

candidates.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

candidates.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
candidates.abstract: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. To recover the correct dynamics, KC-Maps satisfies two key properties: (i) it satisfies the boundary conditions, which we incorporate directly into the neural network architecture, and (ii) it respects the Kolmogorov--Chapman equation, which provides an efficient training objective. We empirically demonstrate that KC-Maps learns to integrate the dynamics of peptide molecular systems and outperforms classical molecular dynamics in terms of GPU-hours.

candidates.title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
candidates.abstract: Estimates of when photonic devices outgrow classical simulation are hard to compare: even for single-photon boson sampling, quoted thresholds range from 50 to 98 photons, as they rest on different tasks and assumptions. We propose as a common unit the time a classical computer needs to draw one sample from the device's exact output distribution, up to floating-point rounding. Only exactness applies equally to every kind of light, since the cost of approximate sampling depends on the accuracy required. The simulability frontier is the device size at which our fastest exact sampler produces one sample per second on a fixed machine; this device size increases with better hardware and algorithms. As the time per sample grows exponentially with the number of detected photons, doubling the machine speed moves the frontier by about one photon, whereas a better algorithm changes the growth rate. We measure the frontier with photonic-engines, an open-source GPU library of exact samplers for single photons, entangled photons from quantum emitters, vacuum-single-photon superpositions and squeezed light. Each sampler is validated against a simulator sharing no code with it. On one NVIDIA H100 GPU, with Haar-random interferometers, twice as many modes as photonic inputs and photon-number-resolving detectors, the frontier lies at 38.3 single photons and at 31.0 entangled photons from one emitter. For squeezed light, a timing model fitted to measurements places it at 41.5 squeezed photonic inputs of mean photon number 0.5. For our samplers, coherence alone makes simulation harder: sources that emit a photon with probability one half reach 64.2 when vacuum and photon are mixed incoherently, as for lossy single photons, but only 50.0 when they are in coherent superposition. Feed-forward from mid-circuit measurement of up to three modes lowers the single-photon frontier only from 38.3 to 38.1.

candidates.title: Mapping of Spacetimes with Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: Gauge freedom in numerical relativity complicates the interpretation of simulation coordinates and the comparison of different descriptions of the same spacetime. We present a data-driven neural network method for learning coordinate maps from numerical metric data to a prescribed target gauge. The network is trained by matching the transformed source metric to the target metric, without assuming a functional form for the coordinate transformation. We first validate the method on analytical Schwarzschild and Kerr geometries, recovering known transformations up to the isometries of the target spacetime. We then apply it to numerical black hole evolutions in moving-puncture coordinates. For a non-spinning black hole, the learned map relates the time-dependent numerical metric to a stationary Schwarzschild metric in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates. For a spinning puncture, the method provides an approximate identification with a Kerr background despite departures from Kerr in the numerical spacetime. We use this identification to construct curvature perturbations and evolve them with the Teukolsky equation, obtaining waveforms that closely match those extracted from the full nonlinear simulation. These results demonstrate that learned coordinate maps can relate numerical spacetimes to analytical backgrounds, with potential applications to cross-code validation and black hole perturbation theory.

candidates.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
candidates.abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

candidates.title: Distributed Global Pose Synchronization for Heterogeneous Multiple Rigid Body Systems on SE(3)
candidates.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of global pose synchronization for heterogeneous multiple rigid-body systems evolving on the matrix Lie group $\SE(3)$. We first construct a new potential function on $\SE(3) \times \mathbb{R}$ with a generalized non-diagonal weighting matrix, together with a set of switching variables governed by continuous-discrete hybrid dynamics. Based on this new potential function and these switching variables, we propose a distributed hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative pose on $\SE(3)$ and group velocity measurements, endowed with global asymptotic stability guarantees. We then further propose a distributed velocity-free hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative and absolute pose measurements, without requiring group velocity measurements, while preserving global asymptotic stability. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed distributed hybrid control schemes.

candidates.title: High Pressure Material Phase Identification with Gaussian Kernel Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: Phase identification is a computational task involving the classification of material structure using the positions of atoms. Using data from Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, our task is to identify the material phase of a set of atoms, based on how the simulations predict their positioning relative to each other. By leveraging existing research on mechanistic neural network theory, particularly Neural Tangent Kernels (NTK), we develop a new and efficient method for classifying simulated material samples. Our method involves defining a set of "atom detectors" that are given positions around the origin in cartesian coordinates. The sum of Gaussians centered at each atom is calculated at each atom detector, and is used as the input to a neural network. We present theoretical and experimental evidence to show that this method is highly effective and efficient at the task. Our method obtains better or similar accuracy scores to commonly used methods while having a major computational speedup.

candidates.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
candidates.abstract: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

candidates.title: Quantum Simulation of Quantum Channels and Applications
candidates.abstract: We review the basic theory of quantum channels and develop a strategy for simulating them on digital quantum computers, drawing upon the \emph{Choi-Kraus operator-sum representation} and Stinespring dilation to provide a unified approach for various applications. We discuss three types of applications, offering explicit examples for each: the preparation of mixed states, measurements described by positive operator-valued measures (POVMs), and the simulation of the evolution of Markovian quantum systems. We recover fundamental concepts from quantum theory, such as the purification of a mixed state and the Naimark dilation associated with a POVM. Regarding the simulation of the evolution of a Markovian quantum system, we introduce an operator, termed the residual operator, to construct, from the system's Liouvillian, a quantum channel that serves as a first-order approximation of the quantum dynamical semigroup. This allows the simulation of quantum dynamics to be performed in a manner analogous to the Euler method for ordinary differential equations, avoiding Trotterization. We prove all the theoretical results mentioned, with the exception of the fundamental Choi-Kraus theorem concerning the operator-sum representation of quantum channels, for which we provide the appropriate references. The explicit simulations discussed were implemented using the AerSimulator from IBM's Qiskit SDK, with the corresponding code available on GitHub.

candidates.title: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
candidates.abstract: Estimating out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in individual instances of random quantum circuits has been proposed as a candidate for verifiable quantum advantage, and demonstrated to be hard for conventional classical algorithms such as tensor networks and Monte Carlo. Using insights from quantum chaos, we develop and implement a polynomial-time classical algorithm for the four-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and the eight-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in typical instances of one-dimensional (1D) quantum circuits. Our results demonstrate average-case classical tractability of estimating OTOCs in the sensitive regime where circuit-to-circuit fluctuations are large. Our algorithm organizes the OTOC into a rapidly converging series, where the leading term includes contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom in the replicated Hilbert space, and subleading terms arise from excursions outside this space. Although chaos is often viewed as an insurmountable barrier to classical simulation, our algorithm exploits a form of dephasing caused by chaos, which suppresses the subleading terms. We provide strong theoretical and numerical evidence to support this suppression. Further, we demonstrate that practical implementations of our algorithm estimate ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in 1D circuits with high accuracy, achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio at larger circuit depths compared to recent 2D experiments by Google. Extending our algorithm to higher dimensions, and resolving the status of quantum advantage in 2D OTOCs, remain open problems.

candidates.title: Legendre manifolds generated by the Barenblatt equations
candidates.abstract: The paper is devoted to the construction of exact general solutions of the equations of oil filtration in a porous medium under the action of an active reagent injected into the reservoir. The choice of the reagent solution determines the control process of chemical oil flooding in hard-to-recover fields. The problem is described by a system of two first-order nonlinear partial differential equations (the Barenblatt model). Conditions are found on the Buckley--Leverett function, the adsorption function, and the distribution function of the reagent in oil under which the original system, by means of a nonlinear change of variables on a five-dimensional manifold endowed with a contact structure, is reduced to a linear wave system with constant coefficients. Six families of such functions are indicated. For them, contact transformations and Legendre surfaces corresponding to general solutions in implicit form are constructed.

candidates.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
candidates.abstract: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions. Learning from them requires recovering motion from completed interactions and using it to anticipate what could happen next. We present $\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching, we train a single model for several prediction tasks: forecasting future interactions, predicting hand motion given object motion or vice versa, generating both trajectories toward a desired final object pose, and completing partially observed interactions. We explicitly model hand-object relations and incorporate contact constraints to help preserve grasp relationships during motion. To obtain 3D supervision from internet videos, we develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to reconstruct completed interactions. We combine these recovered trajectories with annotated interaction datasets as training data for all tasks. We demonstrate strong performance across all tasks, outperforming released forecasters on datasets with 3D annotations. Moreover, we show geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment. Videos are available at https://grasping-the-future.github.io.

candidates.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
candidates.abstract: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. In A1795, AGN feedback dominates the velocity dispersion in the core, similar to Perseus, and may provide turbulent heating at a rate comparable to radiative cooling. In contrast, we obtain only an upper limit on the AGN feedback contribution in A2029, where merger-driven motions dominate. Tailored simulations indicate that an off-axis minor merger $\simeq1.6$ Gyr ago displaced the central low-entropy gas in A2029, potentially suppressing AGN activity. This gas is now returning to the center, possibly facilitating the re-establishment of AGN feedback. We propose an evolutionary view of the double-cascade scenario, in which merger-driven motions dominate during and shortly after significant mergers, while feedback-driven turbulence re-emerges in cluster cores as systems relax. This framework provides a basis for interpreting XRISM kinematic measurements of (weak) cool-core clusters. Our findings highlight the importance of spatially resolved gas kinematics and detailed modeling for identifying double-cascade features and disentangling the contributions of AGN feedback and mergers.

candidates.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
candidates.abstract: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

candidates.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

candidates.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
candidates.abstract: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1\% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $μ\text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

candidates.title: Change-point analysis of textual data: a flexible approach
candidates.abstract: We propose a CUSUM-based change-point procedure for word-frequency vectors that accounts for the variation in the amount of observed textual information over time. Under a multinomial model, we derive the asymptotic null distribution of the proposed statistic, allowing for varying document numbers and lengths. With trimming based on cumulative word counts, the limiting null distribution does not depend on the temporal distribution of textual information. We also consider parametric and nonparametric bootstrap procedures for finite-sample calibration. A simulation study examines their performance under both multinomial sampling and Dirichlet mixtures of multinomial distributions. The results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach under increasing document intensity and show that resampling entire documents provides more reliable calibration in the presence of document-level heterogeneity. Finally, we apply the procedure, combined with binary segmentation, to 68,542 abstracts from the arXiv category stat.ML spanning 2007-2025, identifying multiple changes in word-usage patterns.

candidates.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
candidates.abstract: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe bottleneck: ground-truth deformation fields are notoriously difficult to obtain for real data. We present 2D Gum-Net, an end-to-end architecture that predicts dense elastic deformation fields fully unsupervised. We transfer the Geometric Unsupervised Matching Network (Gum-Net), originally developed for 3D subtomogram alignment in cryo-electron tomography, to 2D elastic registration: all three modules are redesigned in 2D, and the rigid transformation head is replaced by a Dense Spatial Transformer that regresses a sparse control-point grid, lifted to a full-resolution field $Φ$ by bicubic interpolation. Downsampling uses DCT spectral pooling, implemented as frozen-basis matrix multiplications ($\approx 50\times$ GPU speedup), preserving the fine, quasi-periodic structure that max and average pooling destroy. We evaluate on contact-based fingerprints, a challenging testbed for this task: locally self-similar ridge patterns make correspondence maximally ambiguous, skin pressed against a sensor generates authentic large-displacement elastic distortion, and minutiae act as precise landmarks through which an independent matcher externally verifies the topological correctness of predicted fields. Trained purely on synthetic impressions and evaluated zero-shot on real benchmarks, our method improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004 and raises genuine match scores under an independent matcher while leaving imposter scores essentially unchanged. This suggests that the predicted deformations restore true structure without fabricating correspondences.

candidates.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
candidates.abstract: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $Δ^2_{h,2}/Δ^2_h\simeq0.04\,Δ^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $Δ^2_ζ=c_wΔ_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4ε$, and $n_T=-2ε$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $ζ$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $μ$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.
